newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Fuel Oil - Steady as physical players return.
newsitem.headline: Asia Fuel Oil - Steady as physical players return.

text.p: Singapore high sulphur fuel oil was steady on Monday as physical players emerged to draw up the trading boundaries after leaving it to the swaps market on Friday which had led to a late day sell off, traders said.
Traders said the wide bid and sell price on the physical market is evidence of the players' reluctance to make a deal, except to preserve each other's positions.
A European major offered a 20,000 tonne cargo for September 13-17 lifting at $105.00 per tonne against a bid from a Dutch trader at $103.00 for September 11-15.
Traders said the market fundamentals were unchanged amid fairly tight supplies due to improved bunker sales and steady exports from the Middle East.
Singapore stocks were replenished last week following the arrival of several cargoes from the Middle East totalling more than 250,000 tonnes.
Bunker traders said most of the cargoes that were shipped were of a higher viscosity than the 180-cst which is fairly tight and several bunker traders have raised their offers of this grade.
But shipowners did not buy any of the 180-cst that were offered at about $1.00 more than Friday at $110 per tonne.
Swaps trading was steady with September ending 25 cents higher than Monday at $103.75/$104.25.
Indonesia's September allocation of low sulphur waxy residue is due later this week with traders expecting the same volume as for August of 2.7 million barrels.
"It should be around the same as August...around three million including a roll-over of 200-400,000 barrels from August," a Japanese trader said.

Additional August supplies remained unsold as Japanese demand has not taken off as expected in the traditional peak summer season when utiltiy demand increases, as there are good supplies of hydropower, traders said.
The premiums to Pertamina's formula were assessed at 50 to 60 cents per barrel, fob.
